truth.impact: When the destination is unwritable (missing dir, permission denied, disk full) the export reports success with a path that holds no snapshot; syncPinnedSnapshot(dir, true) and any caller tell the operator the catalog is pinned when it is not, and the later offline fallback silently finds nothing.

decoys.problem: removeProviderCatalogEntry swallows every lock/write error in a catch that holds only a comment.
decoys.impact: A prune that fails leaves the entry in the cache without telling the caller.
decoys.quote: // Best-effort, like every other write in this module.
decoys.why_not_a_defect: This is the module's consistent, documented posture: every cache writer (saveProviderCatalogCache, clearProviderCatalogCache, updateProviderCatalogEntry) is best-effort because the cache is a courtesy. The JSDoc states the reason and it holds: the next full refresh writes only the providers it looked at, so an undropped entry is not carried over and ages out. The import result does not claim pruning happened, so no caller is misled.

candidate.problem: exportProviderCatalogSnapshot swallows a failed snapshot write in an empty catch with no comment, then returns `{ ok: true, path: destPath, summary }` as though the file was written. This is the BAD example in error-handling.mdc Rule 3 / Iron Law 1, and it contradicts the function's own doc comment, which says it throws so that a caller never believes it holds the operator's providers.
candidate.impact: Callers are told the pin succeeded when it did not. syncPinnedSnapshot(dir, true) returns the summary, and loadOrRefreshWith (provider-catalog.ts:270) carries on believing a pinned copy exists. The later empty-refresh fallback (provider-catalog.ts:274) then finds no pinned file and serves an empty catalog. The offline fallback the feature exists to provide fails silently. Other sites: none. A search for `catch (e) {}` in the new file finds only this one.

candidate.problem: A missing or non-object `catalog.providers` is quietly turned into `{}`. Every other bad envelope field throws (version, catalog). An empty collection is also how this code signals failure, and a caller reads it as a valid 'snapshot lists zero providers' (error-handling.mdc Rule 1).
candidate.impact: With `prune: true`, a malformed snapshot such as `{"version":1,"catalog":{}}` imports nothing. The prune loop at line 134 then calls removeProviderCatalogEntry for every cached provider, which wipes the operator's cache instead of rejecting the file. Today no in-repo caller passes `prune`, so this is minor. It becomes a data-loss path as soon as one does.
candidate.quote: const providerRecord = typeof rawProviders === "object" && rawProviders !== null ? (rawProviders as Record<string, unknown>) : {};

candidate.problem: Stale doc comment. It says a cache entry newer than the snapshot's copy is kept and only older or missing entries are replaced. The loop actually calls updateProviderCatalogEntry for every accepted entry (line 129), and that function overwrites unconditionally (`providers: { ...current.providers, [entry.name]: entry }`, provider-catalog-cache.ts:234), with no fetchedAt comparison anywhere.
candidate.impact: A reader or caller who trusts the comment will assume an import cannot clobber fresher live data. In fact, importing an old snapshot replaces newer cache entries.
candidate.quote:
An entry already in the cache that is newer than the snapshot's copy

If the save just failed on a first run (lock timeout of 250 ms, unwritable dir), the export throws and loadOrRefreshWith rejects even though `fresh` is a valid catalog.
